purpose: Screen official debt-service sources relevant to the household-consumption and credit-risk mechanisms without constructing a synthetic debt-service variable or estimating any behavioural equation.

bis_sectoral_dsr.current_dataset_scope: The current BIS DSR overview states that total private-non-financial-sector DSRs cover 32 economies, while household and NFC breakdowns are estimated for 17 economies.
bis_sectoral_dsr.consequence: No BIS household or NFC sector DSR may be treated as an exact Romania source. A total-PNFS DSR, if available for Romania, would still not be definitionally interchangeable with a household or NFC sector burden.

bnr_household_dsti.concept: BNR bank-average debt service-to-income (DSTI) levels for new and outstanding housing-loan portfolios

evidence.finding: The report explicitly states 2024 Q1 bank-average DSTI of 34 percent for new housing loans and 41 percent for outstanding/total housing loans.
The report explicitly states 2024 Q2 bank-average DSTI of 34.6 percent for new housing loans and 41 percent for outstanding/total housing loans.
The report explicitly states 2024 Q3 bank-average DSTI of 34.8 percent for new housing loans and 40.9 percent for outstanding/total housing loans.
The report explicitly states 2025 Q2 bank-average DSTI of 37 percent for new housing loans and 42 percent for outstanding housing loans.

semantic_boundary: The published BNR level measure is explicitly tied to housing/mortgage loan portfolios reported by respondent banks; it is not the BIS macro flow-to-flow DSR for the full household sector.
New-loan DSTI is an origination-state measure and cannot stand in for debt service on the outstanding household debt stock.
Outstanding housing-loan DSTI is closer to a borrower-burden state but remains a bank-loan portfolio measure, not total household debt service divided by aggregate household income.
BNR BLS P0303/P1103 are changes in maximum DSTI lending terms reported as net percentages and are not these DSTI level observations.
BNR housing-loan DSTI may become an observed alternative borrower-burden state only under a separately frozen candidate-family measurement contract.
bnr_household_dsti.provider_note: Official BNR report text directly confirms multiple quarterly DSTI level observations and the charts show a longer quarterly history, but no exact machine-readable longitudinal level series has yet been retained. Chart digitisation remains prohibited.

shared_prohibitions: Do not construct a Romania household or NFC DSR from debt stock, a new-business rate and an assumed maturity.
Do not use household debt-to-income as debt service.
Do not use a regulatory DSTI cap as an observed time series.
Do not substitute BNR new-loan DSTI for an aggregate household debt-service burden.
Do not digitise report charts to manufacture a canonical time series.
Do not drop the debt-service term merely because the exact registered concept is unavailable.

household_consumption_response.next_gate: Retain an exact machine-readable BNR housing-loan DSTI level history, separately for new and outstanding loans, or preregister a publication-text-only alternative borrower-burden candidate family with an explicit observation window. Neither path identifies the registered macro household DSR automatically.

credit_risk_npl_response.next_gate: Do not use household DSTI as the debt-service variable for aggregate NPL risk. Reopen only with a debt-service measure aligned to the chosen borrower/portfolio boundary.
